born: 1296 (c.; the brief gives 1296; a secondary source gives 1297)
died: 1359 (per the brief; the Scribd/Sahas article gives 1360; date not checked against a primary source)
role_place: Archbishop of Thessalonica; captured by the Turks at Gallipoli on 10 March 1354 and held in Bithynia (Lampsakos, Pegai, Prusa, Nicaea) for about a year.
why_relevant: Post-1054 Orthodox author who wrote from Ottoman captivity about Christians and Turks and about his debates with Muslim interlocutors on Christ and Muhammad.
fame: Canonised saint and central figure of the hesychast controversy; his captivity letter (Ἐπιστολὴ πρὸς Θεσσαλονικεῖς) and the dialogue with the Chionai are cited in scholarship on Byzantine-Ottoman contact (Arnakis 1951, Meyendorff 1964, Russell 2020, Fazlioğlu 2017), but they are far less known than his hesychast writings. In the scholarship I read, the letter is cited for its narrative of captivity, not for quotable doctrinal lines.
